Cement A: From Monthly Reports to Yearly Profit
Monthly data
Check the volume drop in Tir against the material announcements: summer power limits; temporary.
The price is 15% above Farvardin; compare it with the commodity exchange price.
Normal yearly volume: months without limits about 128 thousand tonnes × 12, minus 2 limited months at 25% less → about 1,472 thousand tonnes.
At the current price of 2,300 → sales of about 3,390 billion rials.
5-year gross margin 35%, admin costs 5% of sales, tax 25% → operating profit about 1,017 and net about 763 billion; 500 million shares → sustainable EPS about 1,525 rials.
FIS point: the Tir drop is no reason to sell because it is temporary and seasonal; but it goes into the yearly model.

For yearly sales volume, which method is more correct?
The average of normal months × 12, minus the effect of the limited months

Normal volume, not the worst or best month.
Holding B and Petrochemical C
Holding B: Separate the One-Off Profit
EPS went from 400 to 1,100 and channels talk of a P/E of 4.
In the other-income note: a gain on selling 20% of a subsidiary’s shares, 750 rials per share.
Normal EPS = 1,100 − 750 = 350; at a price of 4,400 the real P/E is 12.6, not 4.
For a holding the main measure is NAV; if the sale was below the market price, value was destroyed.
Petrochemical C: An Announcement That Changes Profit
Announcement: the gas feedstock price rises 15% from next month.
Sales 20,000, feedstock 10,000, other 4,000 → operating profit 6,000 billion.
Yearly effect: 10,000 × 15% = 1,500 → operating profit 25% lower.
9 months of the year are left → this year’s effect about 1,125 and next year in full.
The change repeats; update sustainable EPS and payback the same day.
Reported EPS is 1,100, of which 750 rials come from selling subsidiary shares. Normal EPS?
Price 4,400 and normal EPS 350. The real P/E?
Yearly feedstock is 10,000 billion and its price rises 15%. The yearly effect on operating profit (billion rials)?
Operating profit was 6,000. What percent of it is this 1,500?
9 months of the financial year are left. This year’s effect (billion rials)?
What kind of change is the feedstock price announcement?
Recurring; update sustainable EPS the same day
One-off; ignore its effect
It only affects this year and reverses next year
Not updating the model after a permanent announcement is a common mistake.
Parts Maker D and Pharma E
Parts Maker D: Profit Without Money
Net profit positive and growing three years in a row.
But operating cash is negative, receivables from a related carmaker went from 6 to 11 months of sales, bank debt doubled, and the auditor has a qualification about collecting receivables.
FIS conclusion: the accounting profit is real but doesn’t reach shareholders; finance costs are growing and a capital increase to cover debt is likely. Off the list.
Pharma E: A Capital Increase That Builds Growth
A 50% increase from cash contributions (500 billion) for a new line with an estimated yearly profit of 180 billion (36%).
Check: the product’s pricing licence (drug prices are set by the government), whether the previous project was on time, and buying imported equipment at the official exchange rate.
Even with 30% less profit the return is about 25%; if that is above the current E/P it creates value. A year’s delay only pushes its arrival back.

The 7 Update Steps
For every new report
1. Classify: monthly, quarterly, material, meeting, capital increase?
2. Number against expectation: compare with your own forecast.
3. Rial effect: what percent of yearly operating profit?
4. Permanent or temporary: only permanent changes change sustainable EPS.
5. Update the model: sustainable EPS, payback, expected return against Akhza.
6. Compare with the portfolio rule: does the reason for buying still hold? Should the weight change?
7. Record it in the journal, before any action. A change under 5% usually needs no action.

A report changes sustainable EPS by 3%. What do you do?
Record it in the journal; usually no action is needed
Sell half the stock at once to cut risk

Acting on changes under 5% is a common mistake.
Temporary changes (such as a month of power cuts) change sustainable EPS.
Only permanent changes change sustainable EPS; temporary ones go into this year’s model.
Step two means comparing with what?
Your own forecast, recorded before publication
The forecasts of channels and other analysts following the report
Yesterday’s share price and the market’s reaction
That’s why you write the forecast before publication.
Explain why the “permanent or temporary” step matters in an update.

Only permanent changes change sustainable EPS and value. A temporary event such as a month’s production stop or a one-off gain shouldn’t lead to a big decision; otherwise you buy and sell emotionally on every piece of news.
Only a permanent change changes sustainable EPS and value
A temporary or one-off event shouldn’t create a big decision
Most news is temporary; a change under 5% usually needs no action.
Analysing a Real 6-Month Report
Summary

Net profit grew 149%, but almost all of it came from a 41% fall in cost of sales; sales grew only 3.5%. Until the reason for the cost drop and the near-zero tax is clear, don’t treat the EPS of 472 as sustainable.
Real sales fell: 3.5% nominal growth with inflation of 30 to 45% means a real fall of about 20 to 29%.

Four explanations for the cost drop: (a) cheaper materials, (b) a higher-margin mix, (c) inventory build-up that moves fixed overhead into inventory, (d) a one-off item such as a reversed write-down. The first two are sustainable, the last two are not.
The Other Lines
Period costs grew faster than sales: admin 46%+, other 53%+.
Non-operating is small and healthy: of 472 rials, 463 is operating. Finance costs halved (probably debt paid off with the capital-increase money).
Effective tax 0.8%: an exemption. At 25%, this period’s EPS would be 357.

The 29% capital increase: last year’s EPS (243) is calculated on 3,500 billion and not adjusted. If it had come from retained earnings, 189 should have been shown; so it was probably a cash contribution. The meaningful growth for shareholders is 94%, not 149%.
Depending on two open questions, six-month profit is between 128 and 472 rials; doubling 472 for the full year is the same mistake as Holding B.
